subject: ClearBridge: error-rate increase and reserved-slot deficit — urgent exec escalation
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@clearbridge.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-01-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Significant error/latency spike from ClearBridge prod (observability attached)

Hi Kimberly / David,

We started seeing a spike in generation errors and 95th percentile latency on our ClearBridge production deployment starting ~08:50 PST. Error rate jumped from ~0.2% to 3.8% and p95 latency went from ~220ms to ~1.1s. This coincided with a rise in queued requests reported on our side.

I've attached a short telemetry snapshot (clearbridge-telemetry-2028-01-14.png) and the reserved-slot usage CSV. The CSV shows our reserved capacity appears to be fully utilized but the API is returning 502/504s and elevated 429s intermittently.

Can you confirm whether this is an internal scheduling/eviction issue or if we hit a hard reserved throughput ceiling? Our SLA window is at risk today. Please escalate as needed — we are on the signoff path for a renewal and need immediate mitigation options.

Thanks,
Alice
Senior Platform Ops
ClearBridge Analytics

(Attachment: clearbridge-telemetry-2028-01-14.png)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: david.kim@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: alice.chen@clearbridge.com
Date: 2028-01-14T09:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Significant error/latency spike from ClearBridge prod (observability attached)

Team — escalating. Summary: ClearBridge reports error-rate ~3.8%, p95 ~1.1s; their reserved-slot usage shows saturation and our telemetry indicates high queue depths on the dedicated GPU pool serving their reservation.

Immediate asks:
- Ops: confirm whether we have any node-level OOMs, preemption events, or noisy-neighbor oversubscription in the region serving ClearBridge. (David)
- SRE: pull the slot allocation timeline and recent placement changes for their reserved capacity (Marissa).
- Commercial: prepare a short customer note with mitigation options + ask for permission to failover non-critical routes to a compatible hosted instance and offer temporary burst credits (Grace).

Options for consideration (fast->slow):
1) Emergency burst authorization (12–24h) to allow ClearBridge to absorb current backlog while we triage.
2) Immediate soft-fallback: route low-priority inference types to hosted variants for short window. Impacts: nominal quality delta; reduces reserved-slot pressure.
3) Accelerate provisioning of 2 additional reserved slots (procurement lead time ~48h) and enable aggressive autoscaling in the dedicated pool.

Please reply with availability for a 09:50 bridge. I've CC'd Alice for transparency. Attachments forwarded: reserved_usage_snapshot-2028-01-14.csv

Kimberly
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: reserved_usage_snapshot-2028-01-14.csv)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, alice.chen@clearbridge.com
Date: 2028-01-14T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Significant error/latency spike from ClearBridge prod (observability attached)

On Tue, Jan 14, 2028 at 09:12 AM Alice Chen <alice.chen@clearbridge.com> wrote:
> We started seeing a spike in generation errors and 95th percentile latency...

Quick technical readout:
- Root signal: sustained queue depth increase on the ClearBridge reserved pool starting 08:40 PST. Queue depth peaked at ~1,800 requests in flight; normal is <200.
- Cause: a mix of short high-concurrency bursts from a nightly batch plus an unindexed prompt pattern that increases KV-cache churn. The serving nodes are hitting CPU+memory pressure during attention kernels (we saw elevated CPU steal on some hosts). No OOMs or preempts in the last 3h.
- Reserved throughput shortfall: their observed effective throughput is ~22% below their committed slot capacity due to queueing/latency (tokens/sec drop). This looks like saturation rather than token-accounting misreporting.

Immediate mitigations I can enact now (with approval):
- Authorize emergency burst: open N extra burst slots (suggest 40% of their commit) for 12 hours. This will reduce queue depth while we patch placement/anti-affinity heuristics.
- Apply short-term routing policy: move non-critical model variants to hosted pool and pin critical low-latency paths to their reserved slots.
- Push a KV-cache retention tweak and a fast path for long-context prompts (reduces overhead for their batch).

If exec authorizes burst credit, I'll trigger and monitor metrics + set automatic rollback in 2h if no improvement.

David
VP, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

(Internal note: provisioning 2 reserved slots would help but procurement ETA is ~48–72h; burst authorization is fastest.)

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@clearbridge.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-01-15T15:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Significant error/latency spike from ClearBridge prod (observability attached)

Thanks Kimberly / David — we appreciate the quick triage. We approve the temporary failover of non-critical routes to hosted variants and accept a 12-hour emergency burst to stabilize traffic.

Two asks from our side:
1) Please confirm times and expected impact (p95 target) once burst is active.
2) We need a short note from Redwood on how this will be handled in our renewal: specifically, whether temporary bursts are credit-eligible and how remedial provisioning will be prioritized.

I'll be on the 16:00 PST bridge if helpful.

Best,
Alice
Senior Platform Ops
ClearBridge Analytics
